title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Labor and Social Security, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Health, and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Issuing the Implementation Measures for the Implementation Plan of Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities during the 11th Five-Year Plan Period
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate
Ministry of Public Security Ministry of Justice Ministry of Civil Affairs
Ministry of Labor and Social Security Ministry of Education Ministry of Health
China Disabled Persons' Federation

Circular on Printing and Distributing the "Implementation Measures for the 'Eleventh Five-Year Plan' Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities"

CDPF Document [2008] No. 3

To the people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security departments (bureaus), judicial departments (bureaus), civil affairs departments (bureaus), labor and social security departments (bureaus), education departments (education commissions), health departments (bureaus), and disabled persons' federations of all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and cities with independent planning status; the Disabled Persons' Working Committee of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; and the Disabled Persons' Working Committee of the General Bureau of Reclamation of Heilongjiang Province:

In order to effectively promote the legal aid work for persons with disabilities during the 'Eleventh Five-Year Plan' period, in accordance with the "Outline of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan for the Cause of Persons with Disabilities in China" and the "Eleventh Five-Year Plan Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities", we have formulated the "Implementation Measures for the 'Eleventh Five-Year Plan' Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities", which are hereby printed and distributed to you. Please implement them earnestly.

(This document is forwarded to the county level)

February 19, 2008

Implementation Measures for the "Eleventh Five-Year Plan" Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities

To strengthen the legal aid work for persons with disabilities and further promote the development of the cause of persons with disabilities and the protection of their rights and interests, in accordance with the "Outline of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan for the Cause of Persons with Disabilities in China" and the "Eleventh Five-Year Plan Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities", the following implementation measures are formulated:

1. Comprehensive Implementation of Legal Aid Work for Persons with Disabilities

The Party Central Committee and the State Council have shown great concern for and attach great importance to the development of the cause of persons with disabilities and the protection of their rights and interests. They have incorporated the development of the cause of persons with disabilities into the overall national economic and social development plan and placed the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities high on the agenda. Party committees and governments at all levels have taken many significant measures, with relevant departments performing their respective duties and cooperating closely, and with strong support from all sectors of society. As a result, the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities has markedly improved, their legal awareness and awareness of rights protection have generally increased, and their ability to participate in social life has significantly enhanced.

Protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law is the main theme of the work for persons with disabilities and also the starting point and ultimate goal of the cause of persons with disabilities. Comprehensive implementation of legal aid work for persons with disabilities is a scientific method and effective means to protect the rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law. It helps to eliminate discrimination against persons with disabilities, prevent violations of their rights and interests, alleviate the contradiction between supply and demand in legal aid for persons with disabilities, and effectively ensure the enjoyment and realization of all lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

Legal aid for persons with disabilities includes not only judicial aid provided by people's courts and people's procuratorates for persons with disabilities and legal aid provided by legal aid centers for persons with disabilities, but also legal services and assistance provided by departments such as public security, judicial administration, civil affairs, labor security, education, health, and the disabled persons' federations, as well as institutions such as law firms, judicial offices (legal service offices), people's mediation organizations, and notary offices. It also includes legal services and assistance provided by all sectors of society to persons with disabilities in various forms.

People's courts, people's procuratorates, and departments of public security, judicial administration, civil affairs, labor security, education, health, and disabled persons' federations at all levels should fully recognize the significance of legal aid work for the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities and the development of the cause of persons with disabilities. They should perform their duties in accordance with the law, adopt various effective measures, and adhere to the principles of simplicity, effectiveness, and appropriateness, continuously improve and perfect the procedures for legal aid for persons with disabilities, effectively protect all lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities from infringement, meet the legal needs of persons with disabilities to the greatest extent, solve the difficulties faced by persons with disabilities, and promote the continuous development of the cause of persons with disabilities.

2. Establishment of Coordination Mechanisms for Legal Aid Work for Persons with Disabilities

Protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities is a shared responsibility of the state and the whole society. Governments at all levels play a leading role, with relevant departments dividing responsibilities, coordinating comprehensively, and jointly promoting the work. These are the prerequisites and inevitable requirements for doing a good job in legal aid for persons with disabilities. A coordination leadership group for legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be established, composed of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Labor and Social Security, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Health, and the China Disabled Persons' Federation. At the local level, coordination leadership groups for legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be established in the respective regions, composed of the local people's court, people's procuratorate, public security, judicial administration, civil affairs, labor security, education, health, and disabled persons' federation. These groups shall give full play to the functions and roles of the coordination mechanism for legal aid work for persons with disabilities and coordinate relevant departments to jointly carry out legal aid work for persons with disabilities in their regions.

The main responsibilities of the coordination bodies for legal aid work for persons with disabilities are: to study and formulate policies and plans for legal aid work for persons with disabilities in the region; to supervise relevant departments to carry out legal aid work for persons with disabilities in the region in accordance with the law; to coordinate relevant departments to properly handle and resolve major typical cases involving infringement of the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities; and to summarize and disseminate experiences in legal aid work for persons with disabilities.

The coordination bodies for legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall hold at least one plenary meeting each year to summarize the legal aid work for persons with disabilities in the current year and to plan the work for the next year; conduct timely research on legal aid work for persons with disabilities in the region to resolve problems and difficulties existing in the work; and promptly coordinate the resolution of major typical cases involving infringement of the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

3. Improvement of the Legal Aid System for Persons with Disabilities

People's courts, people's procuratorates, and departments of public security, judicial administration, civil affairs, labor security, education, health, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall take concrete and effective measures to continuously improve the legal aid system for persons with disabilities, which is led by the judicial aid of people's courts, the legal aid of people's procuratorates, and the legal services and legal aid of judicial administrative departments at all levels, and supplemented by legal aid provided by relevant administrative organs, disabled persons' federations, and social forces.

(1) People's Courts

People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the "Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs" formulated by the State Council and the "Provisions on Providing Judicial Aid to Parties in Real Financial Difficulties" of the Supreme People's Court, grant deferred, reduced, or exempted litigation costs to eligible disabled parties. For persons with disabilities who have already received legal aid and apply for judicial aid, the corresponding judicial aid shall be granted directly. People's courts at all levels shall simplify the procedures for persons with disabilities to apply for judicial aid and gradually expand the scope of judicial aid for persons with disabilities based on the local economic development level.

When trying cases involving persons with disabilities, the courts shall minimize the need for persons with disabilities to travel. Basic people's tribunals may, based on local actual conditions, accept and hear cases involving persons with disabilities on the spot, conduct mediation on the spot, and conclude the case in court, thereby reducing the litigation burden and lowering litigation costs for persons with disabilities. For persons with disabilities in need, people's courts at all levels shall provide judgments in braille or large print free of charge.

People's courts at all levels shall give full play to the role of the trial function and protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law. If, during the trial of a case, it is discovered that a relevant unit has committed acts that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, the court shall promptly issue judicial recommendations to the relevant unit in accordance with the law and urge it to make corrections.

Within three days from the date of completion of the review of a case initiated by public prosecution, a people's court shall, while informing the disabled defendant of the right to retain a defender, also inform him or her that if in financial difficulty, he or she may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. In cases where a public prosecutor appears in court to support the prosecution, if the disabled defendant has not retained a defender due to financial difficulty or other reasons, the people's courts at all levels may appoint a defender for him or her. Within three days from the date of acceptance of a case of private prosecution, a people's court shall, while informing the disabled private prosecutor and his or her legal representative of the right to retain an agent ad litem, also inform them that if in financial difficulty, they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. If a blind, deaf, or mute defendant has not retained a defender, the people's court shall appoint a defender for him or her. In civil litigation and administrative litigation, if a person with disabilities has not engaged an agent due to financial difficulty, the people's courts at all levels shall inform the party of the right to apply for legal aid in accordance with the law.

(2) People's Procuratorates

Procuratorial organs at all levels shall deeply practice the work theme of "strengthening legal supervision and safeguarding fairness and justice," adhere to the principles of establishing procuratorial work for the public and enforcing the law for the people, effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, provide effective legal aid for persons with disabilities, maintain social stability, safeguard fairness and justice, and promote social harmony.

For various criminal acts that infringe upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, especially major typical cases infringing upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities and cases infringing upon the collective interests of persons with disabilities, efforts shall be intensified to crack down, effectively protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities from infringement. If, during the handling of cases, it is discovered that a relevant unit has committed acts that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, the procuratorate shall promptly issue procuratorial recommendations to the relevant unit in accordance with the law and urge it to make corrections.

For disabled criminal suspects whose circumstances are minor and harm is not great, lenient treatment shall be given in accordance with the law, and efforts shall be made to rehabilitate them and give them an opportunity to reform. When examining the approval of arrest of a disabled criminal suspect, the procuratorate shall comprehensively assess the suspect's social dangerousness based on the nature, facts, and circumstances of the crime and the suspect's subjective malice, to determine whether arrest is necessary. If the adoption of compulsory measures or other compulsory measures would not hinder the smooth progress of litigation, arrest shall not be made. Where arrest is possible but not necessary, arrest shall resolutely not be made. For minor criminal cases committed by persons with disabilities, if the criminal suspect confesses guilt and repents, apologizes, actively compensates for losses and obtains the victim's forgiveness, or if both parties reach a settlement agreement and perform it in good faith, and the social harm is not great, the procuratorate may decide not to arrest or not to prosecute in accordance with the law; if prosecution is indeed necessary, the procuratorate may propose to the people's court lenient treatment in accordance with the law. For minor criminal suspects with disabilities who are juveniles, adhere to the policy of "education, persuasion, and rehabilitation," adopt case-handling methods suitable for their physical and mental characteristics, and handle the matter leniently in accordance with the law. At the same time, strengthen contact and coordination with parents, schools, disabled persons' federations, and other relevant departments to jointly conduct education and assistance work.

For cases of complaint, accusation, or appeal filed by persons with disabilities, priority shall be given to accepting, reviewing, and concluding them as soon as possible. For cases not within the jurisdiction of the procuratorate, they shall be transferred to the competent authority, and the relevant persons shall be informed. Strengthen supervision over prisons, detention centers, re-education through labor institutions, and other places to protect the lawful rights and interests of disabled prisoners, detainees, and persons subjected to re-education through labor.

From the date of the first interrogation of a disabled criminal suspect in accordance with the law or the date of adoption of compulsory measures, the people's procuratorate shall, while informing the disabled criminal suspect of the right to retain a lawyer to provide legal consultation, file appeals and accusations, or apply for bail pending trial, also inform him or her that if in financial difficulty, he or she may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. For cases involving state secrets, the disabled criminal suspect shall be informed that the application for legal aid requires the approval of the investigative authority. Within three days from the date of receipt of the case materials transferred for examination before prosecution, the people's procuratorate shall, while informing the disabled criminal suspect of the right to retain a defender, also inform him or her that if in financial difficulty, he or she may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution; while informing the disabled victim and his or her legal representative or close relatives of the right to retain an agent ad litem, also inform them that if in financial difficulty, they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution.

(3) Public Security Departments

Public security departments at all levels shall intensify the rectification of public security order and effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities. They shall investigate and crack down on various illegal and criminal activities that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law, and adopt preventive measures through publicity to enhance the awareness and ability of persons with disabilities to protect themselves.

Public security departments at all levels shall, based on the actual conditions of their regions, continue to deeply crack down on all types of illegal and criminal activities that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, severely crack down on the use of violence, coercion, and other means to organize persons with disabilities to beg and to force or abduct deaf and mute teenagers to engage in illegal and criminal activities. Criminal offenders and criminal gangs committing such illegal acts shall be dealt with severely and promptly in accordance with the law. They shall implement road traffic safety laws and regulations, safeguard the right of way of persons with disabilities, and severely crack down on acts such as non-disabled persons driving motor vehicles for persons with disabilities that infringe upon the right of way of persons with disabilities.

If a blind person or a deaf-mute person violates public security administration, they may be given a lighter, mitigated, or no punishment in accordance with the law; for other persons with disabilities who violate the provisions on public security administration penalties, the policy of giving priority to education and rehabilitation, supplemented by punishment, shall be followed. Generally, restraints shall not be used when interrogating a disabled criminal suspect; if restraints are necessary due to actual personal dangerousness, they shall be removed immediately after the danger is eliminated.

From the date of the first interrogation of a disabled criminal suspect in accordance with the law or the date of adoption of compulsory measures, the public security department shall, while informing the disabled criminal suspect of the right to retain a lawyer to provide legal consultation, file appeals and accusations, or apply for bail pending trial, also inform him or her that if in financial difficulty, he or she may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. For cases involving state secrets, the disabled criminal suspect shall be informed that the application for legal aid requires the approval of the investigative authority.

(4) Judicial Administrative Departments

Further enhance the awareness of the importance of doing a good job in legal aid for persons with disabilities among staff of judicial administrative departments, legal aid institutions, lawyers, notaries, and basic-level legal service workers, and continuously increase their initiative and conscientiousness. Strengthen coordination and cooperation between judicial administrative departments and courts, disabled persons' federations, sub-districts, village (neighborhood) committees, etc., establish an efficient and convenient working mechanism for protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, and timely understand the new situations, new characteristics, and new demands faced by legal aid work for persons with disabilities. Identify advanced models of providing legal aid, legal services, and legal publicity for persons with disabilities, intensify publicity of the deeds of advanced individuals, and commend relevant institutions and personnel.

Legal aid institutions in various localities shall earnestly study the experience and practices of Panlong District, combined with actual local conditions, continuously explore various ways and methods, improve various measures to "facilitate and assist persons with disabilities," and provide convenient conditions for persons with disabilities to apply for and obtain legal aid. Improve the work network for providing barrier-free legal aid to persons with disabilities, set up liaison departments or workstations for legal aid for persons with disabilities in disabled persons' federations at all levels and in places where persons with disabilities are concentrated, such as grassroots communities, welfare enterprises, and special education schools, equip them with full-time or part-time staff, carry out legal consultation, mediation, document drafting, and other work, and promote the extension of barrier-free legal aid work for persons with disabilities to the grassroots level. Construct and improve barrier-free office reception venues and service facilities to facilitate persons with disabilities seeking help, and adopt measures such as issuing legal aid cards, opening legal aid hotlines, setting up consultation mailboxes, providing door-to-door services, and conducting regular follow-up visits to make it convenient for persons with disabilities to seek legal aid. Effectively improve service levels and ensure the quality and efficiency of legal aid for persons with disabilities.

Give full play to the functional role of legal services, guide and promote lawyers, notaries, and basic-level legal service workers to provide timely, convenient, and efficient legal services for persons with disabilities. Continue to encourage law firms to sign legal service agreements with local disabled persons' federations, set up legal service offices in disabled persons' federations, assign full-time lawyers to work in disabled persons' federations, and provide relevant legal services to persons with disabilities free of charge. Based on actual local conditions, formulate preferential policies for providing legal services to persons with disabilities, and reduce or waive service fees for persons with disabilities who are in financial difficulty but do not meet the conditions for legal aid. Where conditions permit, explore the establishment of special funds to provide appropriate economic compensation to law firms, notary institutions, and legal service institutions that provide legal assistance to persons with disabilities. Actively organize and recommend lawyers to participate in the formulation and revision of laws, regulations, and policies related to the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, promote the legalization process of work for persons with disabilities, encourage notaries to actively provide notarization services for persons with disabilities at their homes, answer notarization legal questions for persons with disabilities, and guide basic-level legal service workers to actively participate in legal aid. Strengthen people's mediation work to effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

Seriously carry out publicity and education on laws and regulations regarding the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, strive to enhance the legal awareness of the whole society in protecting the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, and actively create a good legal atmosphere for the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities. Effectively strengthen legal publicity and education for persons with disabilities, and through various channels and forms, deliver various laws and regulations to the hands of the vast number of persons with disabilities, striving to improve their awareness and ability to protect their own lawful rights and interests in accordance with the law.

(5) Civil Affairs Departments

Civil affairs departments at all levels shall, in accordance with the requirements of national laws, regulations, and policies, effectively protect the rights of persons with disabilities from infringement.

Civil affairs departments shall, in accordance with the policies of implementing guarantees and assistance by category, continuously raise the level of protection and assistance for persons with disabilities; civil affairs departments at all levels shall strengthen the relief work for homeless and begging persons with disabilities; efforts shall be intensified to crack down on acts where social welfare enterprises fail to meet the prescribed ratios and standards for employing persons with disabilities and acts that infringe upon the lawful interests of persons with disabilities.

Civil affairs departments at all levels shall strengthen supervision and inspection of places where persons with disabilities are concentrated, such as social welfare enterprises and social welfare institutions, and effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

(6) Labor and Social Security Departments

Labor and social security departments at all levels shall, in accordance with relevant national laws, regulations, and policies, take concrete and effective measures to promote employment of persons with disabilities.

Labor and social security departments at all levels shall strengthen labor security supervision and law enforcement, investigate and deal with acts of employers violating national labor security laws and regulations and infringing upon the labor security rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law, urge employers to strictly comply with national laws and regulations such as the "Labor Law," "Labor Contract Law," and "Employment Promotion Law," and safeguard the various labor security rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law.

Labor dispute arbitration institutions at all levels shall handle labor dispute cases involving persons with disabilities in accordance with the law, fairly and promptly, and effectively protect the labor and employment rights and interests of persons with disabilities. For letters, visits, appeals, and administrative reconsiderations involving labor employment and social security of persons with disabilities, labor and social security departments at all levels shall handle them promptly and in accordance with the law.

(7) Education Departments

Education departments shall thoroughly implement the relevant provisions of national laws, regulations, and policies concerning the right to education of persons with disabilities, effectively protect the right to education of persons with disabilities, and assist relevant departments in severely cracking down on various acts that infringe upon the right to education of persons with disabilities.

For educational institutions that refuse to admit a person with disabilities who meets the admission conditions, or that discriminate against students with disabilities, the competent education administrative department shall order correction within a time limit; if the circumstances are serious, the persons directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions in accordance with the law. For letters, visits, appeals, and administrative reconsiderations involving the right to education of persons with disabilities, education departments at all levels shall handle them promptly and in accordance with the law.

Education departments shall, jointly with disabled persons' federations, conduct regular inspections of educational institutions for persons with disabilities to ensure that these institutions can effectively protect the various educational rights of persons with disabilities.

(8) Health Departments

Health departments shall, in accordance with national laws, regulations, and policies, implement policies and measures for medical and rehabilitation services for persons with disabilities, strengthen management and guidance of medical and health institutions where persons with disabilities are concentrated, such as psychiatric hospitals, and protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities in accordance with the law.

Health departments at all levels shall take active measures in accordance with the law to encourage medical accident appraisal institutions to reduce or waive appraisal fees for persons with disabilities. For letters, visits, appeals, and administrative reconsiderations involving the medical and rehabilitation rights of persons with disabilities, health departments at all levels shall handle them promptly and in accordance with the law.

(9) Disabled Persons' Federations

IV. Creating a Barrier-Free Environment for Legal Assistance to Persons with Disabilities

A barrier-free environment is the prerequisite and foundation for the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities. A full understanding of the importance of a barrier-free environment and the implementation of the state's relevant regulations and policies on accessibility facilitate the smooth development of legal assistance work for persons with disabilities.

People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative organs, civil affairs departments, labor and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall actively promote barrier-free construction of buildings and facilities. Newly built office premises shall comply with the construction requirements for barrier-free facilities. Where existing office premises do not meet the requirements for barrier-free construction, plans shall be formulated for gradual renovation to better serve persons with disabilities.

People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative organs, civil affairs departments, labor and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall promote barrier-free information access. For relevant policy documents, legal assistance procedures, and important information that should be made public, they shall ensure announcement through media, the internet, radio broadcasts, sign language programs, display screens, and other forms to protect the right of persons with disabilities to be informed. In areas where conditions are genuinely lacking, necessary convenience shall be provided for persons with disabilities to obtain relevant information.

For persons with disabilities who require communication through sign language, Braille, large fonts, captions, interpretation, or other means during the legal assistance process, people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative organs, civil affairs departments, labor and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall provide such accommodations.

In cases involving persons with disabilities, the competent case-handling authority shall strengthen communication and contact with relevant government departments, the disabled persons' federation and other people's organizations, as well as the entity where the person with disabilities works, to fully understand the relevant circumstances of the person with disabilities and effectively protect their lawful rights and interests.

V. Strengthening Supervision and Inspection of Legal Assistance Work for Persons with Disabilities

The coordination leading groups for legal assistance work for persons with disabilities at all levels, as well as the people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative organs, civil affairs departments, labor and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations, shall strengthen supervision and inspection of legal assistance work for persons with disabilities. Through regular inspections, unscheduled inspections, and spot checks, they shall examine the establishment and operation of coordination leading groups for legal assistance work for persons with disabilities; the promulgation of policies on legal assistance for persons with disabilities, the handling of major cases, and the summarization and promotion of experiences; the progress of work by each functional department responsible for legal assistance for persons with disabilities; the establishment and operation of legal assistance centers for persons with disabilities; and relevant work files and statistical records, among other matters. The inspecting department shall, based on the inspection results, put forward corresponding rectification opinions and suggestions, summarize successful experiences, and promote them.

VI. Providing Funding Guarantees for Legal Assistance Work for Persons with Disabilities

Governments at all levels shall include funds for legal assistance for persons with disabilities in their fiscal budgets, attract social resources, strive for relevant project funding, and raise funds through multiple channels for legal assistance work for persons with disabilities. People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, judicial administrative organs, civil affairs departments, labor and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall actively strive for the allocation of special funds for legal assistance work for persons with disabilities. Central funding shall be used primarily for researching and formulating policies on legal assistance for persons with disabilities, providing guidance for carrying out such work, and providing appropriate subsidies for local case-handling expenses in legal assistance for persons with disabilities based on actual circumstances. Local funding shall be used primarily for carrying out local legal assistance work for persons with disabilities and training legal assistance workers for persons with disabilities.
